title: RC Time Constant
summary: the charge/discharge timing of a resistor-capacitor pair and the resulting filter cutoff.
body:
the time constant tau = R * C sets how fast a capacitor charges or discharges
through a resistor. after one tau the capacitor reaches ~63% of the final
voltage; after 5 tau it is within ~1% (considered fully settled). the same RC
pair forms a first-order low-pass (or high-pass) filter with cutoff fc.

tables.title: charge level after n time constants

examples: R = 10k, C = 1 uF: tau = 10ms, fc = 1 / (2*pi*10000*1e-6) = 15.9 Hz low-pass.
debounce: 10k + 100nF gives tau = 1 ms, settling in ~5 ms.
gotchas: electrolytic capacitor tolerance is wide (-20%/+80% on some), so RC timing from them is imprecise
for a high-pass the cutoff formula is the same but output is taken across R, not C
